idea: Client-side advisory for first-time commercial developers
buyer: Business owners developing their own premises
pain: They are spending millions on a building and have no idea what they are doing
verdict: Solvent buyer, high fees, genuine dual-skill need - the best idea in the architecture cluster.

why.distribution: Reachable through her husband's professional network, one introduction at a time.
why.demand: Project managers and client-side advisors are paid for this today.
why.fmf: Understanding both the building and the money is exactly what a first-time developer lacks.
why.revenue_structure: One project per client, spanning many months.
why.defensibility: The dual capability plus accumulated project experience is genuinely scarce.
why.ceiling: £22k x 9 projects = £198k, but each runs 12-18 months so nine concurrent is impossible.

ceiling_arithmetic: £22k x 9 projects = £198k, but a client-side advisory role runs 12-18 months, so nine concurrent projects is not deliverable solo. Realistic: 2-3 = £44-66k.
carries: The one architecture-cluster idea aimed at a buyer with real money and a real need for both her skills.
kills: Project duration. Each engagement consumes months, so the annual client count is structurally tiny.
test: Ask her husband for two introductions to business owners planning premises.
test_pass: One engages for a paid advisory role.
test_fail: They already have a project manager.
